definitions.explanation: A supernatural transformation, especially in folklore where animals or spirits change into human form. Distinct from the common reading へんか (change), this reading specifically refers to magical or supernatural transformation.

definitions.gloss: apparition; phantom; supernatural being in disguise
definitions.explanation: A being that has transformed itself, such as a fox or raccoon dog in Japanese folklore that has taken human form.

examples.japanese: {狐|きつね}の{変化|へんげ}を{見|み}た。
{昔話|むかしばなし}では、{狸|たぬき}が{人間|にんげん}に{変化|へんげ}する。
examples.english: In folktales, raccoon dogs transform into humans.

examples.japanese: {古|ふる}い{寺|てら}の{近|ちか}くで{変化|へんげ}を{見|み}たという{噂|うわさ}が{村中|むらじゅう}に{広|ひろ}まった。
examples.english: A rumor spread throughout the village that someone had seen a shape-shifting apparition near the old temple.

examples.japanese: あれは{変化|へんげ}の{仕業|しわざ}だ。
examples.english: That is the doing of a shape-shifting spirit.

examples.japanese: この{森|もり}には{変化|へんげ}が{住|す}んでいると{言|い}われている。
examples.english: It is said that shape-shifting spirits live in this forest.

examples.japanese: {能|のう}の{演目|えんもく}には、{変化|へんげ}をテーマにしたものが{数多|かずおお}くある。
examples.english: There are many Noh plays with the theme of supernatural transformation.

notes:
READING NOTE:
The same kanji {変化|へんか} read as へんか means ordinary change or alteration. The reading へんげ specifically refers to supernatural transformation in folklore and religion.

CULTURE:
In Japanese folklore, foxes ({狐|きつね}) and raccoon dogs ({狸|たぬき}) are the most famous shape-shifting animals. Buddhist texts also use this term for manifestations of deities ({権化|ごんげ}).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {変化|へんげ}の{術|じゅつ} (the art of transformation)
- {変化|へんげ}する (to transform supernaturally)
- {変化|へんげ}の{仕業|しわざ} (the doing of a shape-shifter)
